feedback.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{6}^{2})$ with $P(X<5)=0.7734,$ find $\mu .$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ | $\,0.7454\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ | $\,0.8051\,$ |

$\mu =$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5)=0.7734\,⇒\,P(X\le 5)=0.7734\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =0.7734 \\ P(Z\le \frac{5-\mu }{6}) & =0.7734 \\ Φ(\frac{5-\mu }{6}) & =0.7734 \\ \frac{5-\mu }{6} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.75)=0.7734\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)=0.75.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-\mu }{6} & =0.75 \\ 5-\mu  & =4.5 \\ \mu  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$
